clue.text: Heads off to deal with this gatekeeper?

definitions.text: Heads off to deal with this gatekeeper?

parts.words: Heads off to deal with this gatekeeper?
parts.note: the gatekeeper of the classical underworld was a dog with three heads, so dealing with him would mean cutting off heads, plural

explanation.surface: A guide on how to get past a doorman: knock his head off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heads' is the joke: one head off would not do for the three-headed hound of Greek myth, so the plural points to the many-headed guard.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the three-headed hound guarded the entrance to Hades, keeping the dead from leaving.

clue.text: Tax department underwriting American shows

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece written under another sits below it, so the tax office comes after the abbreviation

parts.note: the IRS is the Internal Revenue Service, the US tax authority

explanation.surface: An American tax office insures and promotes some broadcasts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underwriting' looks like insurance jargon, but in a down clue it just means writing underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: To air a programme is to broadcast or display it, so the verb form matches shows.

clue.text: Screenings of birthmarks essentially down by 88%

indicators.note: the essential, central letter of the birthmark word is the Roman numeral for fifty; cutting fifty by 88% leaves six, so it becomes the numeral for six

parts.note: moles are small dark marks on the skin, often present from birth

explanation.surface: A statistic about how often birthmarks are shown on screen falling sharply.
explanation.walkthrough: The central L is 50 in Roman numerals; 50 reduced by 88% is 6, written VI, which replaces the L in MOLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Films are what get screened, so screenings in a loose plural sense are cinema pictures.

clue.text: Embrace special powers to oversee Yorkshire Water?

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece overseeing another sits above it, so the powers come first

parts.note: ESP is extrasensory perception, supposed special mental powers
the Ouse is a river flowing through York in northern England

explanation.surface: Someone wants special powers to supervise the regional water company, Yorkshire Water.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire Water is a real utility firm, but here it is a river in Yorkshire: the Ouse, which flows through York.
explanation.definitionFit: To espouse a cause is to take it up and support it, as one embraces an idea.

clue.text: Creature in a new feature climbing tops of Kensington East

indicators.note: in a down answer, climbing means the letters read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: to star in a show is to feature in it as the lead

indicators.note: the tops of words in a down entry are their first letters

explanation.surface: A creature appears in a new magazine feature on rising Kensington East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climbing' reverses A, N and STAR to give RATSNA; then the first letters of Kensington and East add KE.
explanation.definitionFit: The rat snake is a North American and Asian constrictor that feeds largely on rodents, so it is a type of animal.

clue.text: Highlight is a cute cat leaping across tiny space

indicators.note: the scrambled letters stretch across the small space, so it ends up inside them
leaping suggests the letters jumping about into a new order

parts.note: an en is a printer's space, half the width of an em

explanation.surface: A sweet cat jumping over a small gap is the best bit of the show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaping' rearranges A CUTE CAT into ACCTUATE, and 'across' puts EN inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To accentuate something is to emphasise it, making it stand out, as highlighting does.

clue.text: Luthor perhaps figures in reference books

parts.note: Lex Luthor is Superman's arch-enemy in the comics; 'perhaps' because Luthor is one example of the name
icons are images or figures, as in religious icons

explanation.surface: Superman's villain turns up in some encyclopaedias.
explanation.definitionFit: A lexicon is a dictionary, the classic kind of book consulted for reference.

clue.text: Secrets penned by co-star can alarm

indicators.note: the answer is penned, enclosed, by the words that follow, so it sits within their letters

explanation.surface: Secrets written by a fellow actor can cause alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcana are mysteries or hidden knowledge known only to initiates.

clue.text: Secures sluggish individual cycling

indicators.note: cycling sends the first letter round to the back of the word

parts.note: a snail is proverbially slow, so a sluggish creature

explanation.surface: A slow person gets a lock on a bike while cycling.
explanation.walkthrough: Moving the S of SNAIL from the front to the end gives NAILS.
explanation.definitionFit: To nail something down is to fasten it, so nails is a verb meaning fastens firmly.

clue.text: Soft pencil is required for flyer

parts.note: B marks a soft-leaded pencil; read as the grade 1B, with the figure 1 taken as the letter I

explanation.surface: An artist or pilot needs a soft pencil for some sketch.
explanation.walkthrough: Pencil grades use B for soft (black) lead; the setter treats the softest-but-one grade 1B as IB, which the blog noted is a stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibis is a long-billed wading bird, and as a bird it is something that flies.

clue.text: Papers oddly eschewing coolest pin-ups

parts.note: ID means identity papers

indicators.note: avoiding the odd-numbered letters leaves only the even ones, second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: The newspapers are odd in avoiding the hippest pin-up stars.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the odd letters C, O, E, T of COOLEST keeps O, L, S.
explanation.definitionFit: Pin-ups are celebrities whose pictures fans put on walls, so they are adored stars.

clue.text: Character caught on centre of set in Spartacus?

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another follows it, so the letter and the catch come after the centre
the centre of a three-letter word is its middle letter

parts.note: pi is a Greek letter, and a letter is a character
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: An actor is caught on a film set during the making of Spartacus.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark shows that Spartacus, the 1960 Kubrick film, is an example of the type rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Spartacus is a sweeping historical film of grand scale, the kind called a big-screen spectacle.

clue.text: Clutch starts to eat small crabs

parts.note: to clutch is to grip; as a noun a grip is a hold

indicators.note: the starts of the next words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A clutch of small crabs begins to feed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crabs' looks like the shellfish but is the verb meaning complains.
explanation.definitionFit: To crab is to grumble, so crabs and gripes both mean complains.

clue.text: Release Dynamic Duo in port around Cuba

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go around the island's abbreviation
dynamic suggests motion, so the letters are set moving into a new order

parts.note: C is the international vehicle code for Cuba

explanation.surface: Batman and Robin, the Dynamic Duo, are freed while in a harbour near Cuba.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dynamic' rearranges DUO IN PORT, and 'around' puts C inside to give PRODUCTION.
explanation.definitionFit: A film or show released to the public is a production, so the noun release names one.

clue.text: Most fashionable of stars met cast

indicators.note: to cast is to throw, so the letters are thrown into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: The best-dressed of the celebrities met the actors in a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like the actors in the film but rearranges STARS MET.
explanation.definitionFit: Smart means stylish and well-dressed, so its superlative is the most stylish.

clue.text: Films get lost by vacuous teenagers

parts.note: shoo is said to drive someone away, like 'get lost'

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so the word loses its insides and keeps only its outer letters

explanation.surface: Mindless teenagers have been told to go away from the films.
explanation.definitionFit: To shoot a scene is to record it on camera, so shoots means films as a verb.

clue.text: Chuck supports characters in the same old roles

indicators.note: in a down answer, a supporting piece sits beneath the other, so the throw comes second

parts.note: type is printed characters, as in typeface
to chuck is to throw, and to cast is to throw

explanation.surface: An actor called Chuck backs up the characters, always in familiar parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chuck' looks like a name but is the verb throw.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor who is typecast keeps being given the same kind of part over and over.

clue.text: Fellow confronted about making Java drug-free?

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: to face someone is to confront them

explanation.surface: A man was challenged over making coffee without its stimulant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Java' is slang for coffee, not the island or the programming language; the drug is caffeine.
explanation.definitionFit: Java is slang for coffee, and coffee without its caffeine is the decaffeinated kind.

clue.text: Document mostly deconstructed minor style of drama

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter is kept

parts.note: a file is a document or record

indicators.note: something deconstructed is taken apart, so these letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A paper largely takes apart a minor form of theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: FILE without its last letter is FIL; 'deconstructed' rearranges MINOR into MNOIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Film noir is a cinematic genre of dark, cynical crime dramas, especially 1940s Hollywood ones.

clue.text: Partner once given plenty of warning

parts.note: an ex is a former husband, wife or partner
ample means plentiful, more than enough

explanation.surface: A former spouse was given lots of notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plenty of warning' reads as one phrase but splits: 'plenty' is wordplay and 'warning' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Punishing someone to deter others is making an example of them, so the example serves as a caution.

clue.text: Mash up hare's last bit of appendix for prophet

indicators.note: to mash food is to crush it into a pulp, so these letters are pulped into a new order
the last bit of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A recipe: mash hare with a finishing touch for a seer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mash' rearranges UP HARE'S into HARUSPE; the X ending appendix follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A haruspex was a Roman seer who foretold the future by examining animal entrails.

clue.text: Actor's representation of a well-mannered person

definitions.note: the definition names the representation, the answer the person who provides it

parts.note: a gent, short for gentleman, is a courteous, well-behaved man

explanation.surface: A performer plays a courteous character on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Actor's representation' suggests a role being portrayed, but it is the person who represents an actor in business.
explanation.definitionFit: Performers employ someone to negotiate their contracts and find them work on their behalf.

clue.text: Smugglers left to finish one's healthy breakfast

indicators.note: the letter is taken out and placed at the finish, the end of the word

parts.note: mules are people who smuggle drugs across borders
I is one in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Drug carriers have gone, leaving one to eat a wholesome first meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Drug mules are couriers who smuggle drugs by carrying them; 'left' is both the letter that moves and, in the surface, the verb 'gone'.
explanation.definitionFit: Muesli is a cereal of oats, nuts and dried fruit, eaten as a wholesome morning meal.

clue.text: Movement in Io as possibly captured by thousands

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are captured, held inside, by the thousands

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so two of them for the plural

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Motion on Jupiter's moon Io, perhaps recorded by thousands of observers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges IO AS to AOIS, which 'captured by' puts between M and M.
explanation.definitionFit: Maoism is the political ideology of Mao Zedong, a movement in the sense of an organised cause.

clue.text: Kiss in tense film script

parts.note: T is a grammar abbreviation for tense

indicators.note: in places the kiss inside the other letters

parts.note: ET is Spielberg's 1982 film about an extra-terrestrial
X is a kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A kiss scene in a tense film's screenplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A script is the written words of a play or film, its written content.

clue.text: Company boss limits amateur's brief appearance

indicators.note: the boss's letters form limits on either side of the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: a CEO is a chief executive officer, the head of a company
AM is an abbreviation for amateur; the 's is 'has'

explanation.surface: A chief executive restricts an amateur's short spell on screen.
explanation.definitionFit: A cameo is a small part played by a well-known actor, appearing only briefly.

clue.text: Fluid from bottles maybe working, drip returned

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the letters are read in reverse order

parts.note: on means working, as a machine that is on
an IV is an intravenous drip in hospital

explanation.surface: Fluid from a bottle was working while a hospital drip was put back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returned' reverses ONIV to give VINO.
explanation.definitionFit: Vino is a casual word for wine, a liquid usually sold in bottles.

clue.text: Change direction of film that lacks heart

indicators.note: the word loses its heart, the two central letters

parts.note: a veneer is a thin film or surface layer

explanation.surface: A soulless film changes course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' looks like a movie in this film-themed grid but is a thin surface coating; VENEER without its middle NE gives VEER.
explanation.definitionFit: To veer is to swerve or turn suddenly onto a new course.

clue.text: Duck stopping stops ducks

indicators.note: the letter sits in the word, stopping the flow, inside it

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of zero, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A duck halts as the duck halts, a repetitive tongue-twister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' at the start is the cricket zero and 'ducks' at the end is the verb meaning bends down.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck is to bend down quickly, so ducks means bends forward.

clue.text: Earwig gleaming having shed skin

indicators.note: shedding its skin, the word loses its outer letters at both ends

parts.note: glistening means shining, gleaming

explanation.surface: An earwig is shining after moulting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Earwig' looks like the insect but is a British verb meaning eavesdrop.
explanation.definitionFit: To earwig is to eavesdrop, secretly overhearing a private conversation.
